item.title: Multiple Row Updates in SQL: Efficient Methods Compared
item.description:
“Multiple Row Updates in SQL: Efficient Methods Compared”

How can a database professional efficiently update numerous records in a single SQL operation, especially when the update values are specific to each row identifier? Several strategies exist, each with distinct performance implications and syntactic requirements across different SQL dialects, particularly MySQL/MariaDB.

Primary Methods for Concurrent Row Updates

Several effective approaches surface when tackling bulk updates based on provided data sets:

1. Utilizing INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (MySQL Specific)

This MySQL feature is frequently cited as a concise way to perform upserts (insert if new, update if existing). If a row identified by the primary key or unique index already exists, the UPDATE clause is triggered instead of a standard insertion failure.

item.title: SQL Server Update with Join: Syntax, Best Practices, and Alternatives
item.description:
“SQL Server Update with Join: Syntax, Best Practices, and Alternatives”

Encountering issues when attempting to update a SQL Server table using a join? This post delves into common syntax errors and provides a variety of effective solutions and alternative approaches for updating data across related tables.

A frequent challenge in SQL Server arises from incorrect syntax when performing an UPDATE statement that involves joining two tables. Unlike some other SQL dialects, SQL Server has specific requirements for its UPDATE FROM clause.
